book.why: The page's strongest signal: Ophelia's breakout leader still has room to run (RSI 51, 98.4% of its high), Cecil argues 18.7x understates its earnings at $100 WTI, and both name its negative correlation to SPY as the book's hedge against a hawkish dot plot.

Ophelia's healthcare bounce and Marky's screen (2.1 widths below a channel rising 96% a year) agree it is an oversold pullback in an uptrend on 95% EPS growth; its MACD histogram is still falling, so it sits below XOM.

Ophelia's AI-demand catalyst meets Marky's shallow 0.9-width pullback with a rising MACD histogram, but its 6.32% weekly volatility is the sheet's highest, so it gets the smallest weight of the three names with two backers.
Cecil's money-center bank at 16.4x with 13.4% EPS growth and the sheet's lowest volatility earns more if rates hold near 5% and steadies the book against the rate risk in LLY and AMD.
Cecil's insurer is the sheet's cheapest name with rising EPS (11.5x, +10.1%) and its short-duration float reinvests near 5%, held to 10% because of its 4.45% weekly volatility.

rationale: The core is the three names two members reached by different routes: XOM (Ophelia's breakout, Cecil's value) at the 30% cap, plus LLY and AMD (Ophelia's rotation, Marky's channel screen), sized by volatility. Around that core the book is split across Wednesday's Fed decision: XOM, JPM and PGR earn more if rates stay near 5%, LLY and AMD pay if the hike reads as insurance, and 10% cash absorbs the Fed, BOJ and retail-sales cluster. VLO, VICI, SPG, LYV and CAT are left out.
